title: Brill--Noether existence and rank for graphs through genus six
abstract: This repository proves Baker's Brill--Noether existence conjecture for finite graphs of genus at most six.  The conjecture states that if G is a finite connected loopless multigraph, with genus defined to be g = E-V+1, then for all nonnegative integers d, r, there exists a configuration of d chips on G with Baker--Norine rank at least r provided that the Brill--Noether number rho = g - (r+1)(g-d+r) is nonnegative.  To the author's knowledge, this is a new result, extending a result of Atanasov and Ranganathan from genus five to six.  Two generalizations are also included.  First, in genus at most six, the Brill--Noether rank, in the sense of Lim--Payne--Potashnik, is at least the expected dimension of the Brill--Noether locus, when d is at most g+r. This is a combinatorial analog of the classical lower bound on the dimension of Brill--Noether loci, usually established on algebraic curves using intersection theory.  Second, the Brill--Noether existence conjecture for graphs with one marked vertex, as stated by Pflueger--Solomon, holds in genus up to five.  The proof synthesizes recent work of Christ--Ma and Draisma--Vargas. The work of Christ--Ma predicts the subdivision required to obtain special divisors on graphs, using enumerative geometry. The work of Draisma--Vargas provides a combinatorial construction to realize these special divisors.  The novel contribution in this repository is a descent argument, producing special divisors on the original graph from special divisors on an odd subdivision.  This work has not yet been written up for publication; the present repository is the first announcement of it.
